Memphis printed cotton swatch card

A sample card of Memphis printed cottons under a black header with the group’s blocky wordmark.

Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The V&A records a swatch of printed cottons, Italy, 1985, with Memphis as designer. V&A record.

The record does not name the pattern or the designer of the header card.

Observed

  • A black header strip carries “MEMPHIS” in white, squared capitals with cut and notched strokes.
  • The front swatch shows turquoise squares, tilted at different angles, on a red ground.
  • Behind it, pinked edges of other fabrics show yellow, orange, and black.
  • The swatches are fixed to a plain white card with the accession number written below.

Why it belongs

The letterforms on the header look like Christoph Radl’s 1982 Memphis logotype drawing (record). This is a visual comparison; the V&A does not name the designer.

Tilted squares scattered on a strong ground is the simplest version of the Memphis “confetti” pattern.

Borrow

Scatter one simple shape at random angles over a contrasting solid ground.

Pair a busy pattern with a black band that carries the brand in heavy white lettering.
